courses.title: ESL: Written Communication II
courses.contact_hours: 3-6 credits. 3-6 lecture hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in writing at the low-intermediate level. Improves students' competence in grammatical patterns of written English. Requires practice in writing sentences and longer pieces of writing.

courses.title: ESL: Reading and Vocabulary II
courses.contact_hours: 3-6 credits. Lecture 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction and practice in reading and vocabulary development at the low-intermediate level. Improves students' reading fluency, proficiency, and vocabulary to enable them to function adequately in ESL Level 3 and prepare for college-level reading. Credits are not applicable toward graduation.

courses.title: Oral and Written Communications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practice in the sound, stress, intonation, structural patterns, grammar, vocabulary, and idioms of beginning-level English. Prerequisite: Requires ability to understand short spoken passages as well as familiarity with basic grammatical structure.

courses.title: Composition I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction and practice in the writing process, emphasizing development of fluency in writing and competence in structural and grammatical patterns of written English. Prerequisite: Requires ability to express ideas clearly in writing without a consistent pattern of grammatical errors as indicated by a placement exam or teacher recommendation from a previous level. Credits are not applicable toward graduation.

courses.title: Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Requires competency in reading as indicated by the placement test or by teacher recommendation from a previous level.
courses.description: Helps students improve their reading comprehension and vocabulary development. Improves students' reading proficiency to a level that would allow the students to function adequately in ESL 42 and other college classes.

courses.title: Oral Communications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Requires competency in the English language as indicated by a placement test score or teacher recommendation from a previous level or from other college classes.
courses.description: Helps students practice and improve listening and speaking skills as needed for functioning successfully in academic, professional, and personal settings. Assesses students' oral skills and includes, as needed, practice with pronunciation, rhythm, stress, and intonation. Provides exercises, practices, small and large group activities, and oral presentations to help students overcome problems in oral communication. Credits are not applicable toward graduation.

courses.title: Composition II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides further instruction and practice in the writing process and introduces advanced language patterns. Includes practice in developing and improving writing strategies. Credits are not applicable: Requires a sense of paragraph structure and development, appropriate use of verb forms, and command of basic sentence structures with some coordination and subordination, as indicated by a placement test and writing sample, or teacher recommendation from a previous level. Credits are not applicable toward graduation.

courses.title: Math Applications for ELE/ETR Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents mathematical applications for ELE/ETR students. Includes mathematical concepts and problems in algebra and trigonometry, and direct application to electronic analysis. Includes a survey of advanced mathematics to develop and reinforce electronic concepts.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Fundamentals I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies D.C. and A.C. circuits, basic electrical components, instruments, network theorems, and techniques used to predict, analyze and measure electrical quantities. Part I of II.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Fundamentals II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies D.C. and A.C. circuits, basic electrical components, instruments, network theorems, and techniques used to predict, analyze and measure electrical quantities. Part II of II.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies current flow in direct and alternating current circuits with emphasis upon practical problems. Reviews mathematics used in circuit calculations. Introduces concepts of resistance, capacitance, inductance and magnetism. Focuses on electronics/circuits application.

courses.title: Electronic Applications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 2-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides laboratory and shop experience as applied to basic electronic devices, circuits and systems with emphasis on practical measurements. Part I of II.

courses.title: General Industrial Electronic Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies devices, circuits, power modules, analog and digital, open and closed loop control and servo systems. May include laboratory projects and modular troubleshooting.

courses.title: Electronics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electronic devices as applied to basic electronic circuits and systems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electronic devices as applied to basic electronic circuits and systems. Part II of II.

courses.title: Devices and Applications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Co-requisite: knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Teaches theory of active devices and circuits such as diodes, power supplies, transistors (BJTs), amplifiers and their parameters, FETs, and operational amplifiers. May include UJTs, oscillators, RF amplifiers, thermionic devices and others. Part I of II.

courses.title: Amplifiers and Integrated Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies devices and amplifiers with emphasis on analysis and design. May include summing and integrating amplifiers, choppers, modulators and other circuits.

courses.title: PC Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the maintenance, troubleshooting and repair of personal computer systems. Uses IBM or compatible computer systems to provide fault isolation drill and practice.

courses.title: Machine Control Using Relay & Programmable Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to hardwired relay logic and the programmable logic controller (PLC) as utilized in a variety of different control tasks. Covers different types of inputs and outputs in control system. Teaches practical troubleshooting strategies.

courses.title: Electronic Circuits and Troubleshooting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies analog and digital circuits and systems with standard circuit test and troubleshooting procedures. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Circuits and Troubleshooting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies analog and digital circuits and systems with standard circuit test and troubleshooting procedures. Part II of II.

courses.title: Survey of Microprocessors
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of microprocessor architecture, basic machine language programming, and I/O devices.

courses.title: Upgrading and Maintaining PC Hardware
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches upgrading of the system CPU, memory, drives, multimedia components, modem, and video card in a microcomputer. Covers hardware as well as software related maintenance issues.

courses.title: Digital Circuit Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of digital logic and the study of digital circuits and their applications.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Electronic Devices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory.
courses.description: Studies active devices and circuits such as diodes, power supplies, transistors, amplifiers and others. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronics Diagnostics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches analyzing, testing and repair of fundamental assemblies, subassemblies, circuits and systems as applied to electronic maintenance and manufacturing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Computer Troubleshooting and Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches procedures for isolating and correcting problems in computers and computer-related hardware. Emphasizes operational concepts, use of diagnostic software and troubleshooting equipment.

courses.title: Mechatronic Process Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: MEC 140 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies systems integrating mechanical components with electrical components and logic devices used to control manufacturing operations. Surveys electromechanical actuators, sensors, digital to analog conversion, and methods of computer control as related to the managing and monitoring of manufacturing processes.

courses.title: Industrial Electronics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies linear integrated circuits for industrial applications, motors, industrial control devices, power control circuits, transducers, industrial process control, and sequential process control. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Communications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies noise, information and bandwidth, modulation and demodulation, transmitters and receivers, wave propagation, antennas and transmission lines. Includes broad band communication systems, microwave, both terrestrial and satellite, fiber optics, multiplexing and associated hardware. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Communications II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies noise, information and bandwidth, modulation and demodulation, transmitters and receivers, wave propagation, antennas and transmission lines. Includes broad band communication systems, microwave, both terrestrial and satellite, fiber optics, multiplexing and associated hardware. Part II of II.

courses.title: Solid State Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory, and active devices and circuits.
courses.description: Teaches theory and application of amplifiers and oscillators. Includes amplifier circuit configurations, amplifier classes, operational amplifiers, power amplifiers, bandwidth distortion, and principles of feedback.

courses.title: Microprocessor Application I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the fundamentals of microprocessors including architecture, internal operations, memory, I/O devices machine level programming and interfacing. Emphasizes instrumentation and microprocessor. Part I of II.

courses.title: Microprocessor Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of microprocessors including architecture, internal operations, memory, I/O devices, machine level programming and interfacing.

courses.title: Computer Electronics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of digital electronics and microprocessors to familiarize the student with typical circuits and methods used to interface computer and/or controllers with various I/O devices. Includes exposure to high level programming as well as assembly language routines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Computer Electronics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of digital electronics and microprocessors to familiarize the student with typical circuits and methods used to interface computer and/or controllers with various I/O devices. Includes exposure to high level programming as well as assembly language routines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Digital Principles, Terminology and Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies digital principles, terminology and applications covering number systems, arithmetic, Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps and advanced logic circuits. Includes the study of registers, encoding and decoding, and multiplexing; A/D, D/A, displays and others.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Logic Circuits and Computers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies digital logic, Boolean algebra, and arithmetic circuits, using standard integrated circuits and the functional block approach. Introduces concepts of computers, the internal operation and control language.

courses.title: Digital Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes basic numbering systems, Boolean algebra, logic circuits and systems, pulse circuits and pulse logic systems as applied to computer and microprocessor technology.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Microcomputer Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the student with an exposure to the various techniques and procedures used to troubleshoot a microcomputer. May include an overview of a particular microprocessor system, use of isolation flow charts, test point charts, prints, diagnostic routines, component testing and fault isolation labs.

courses.title: Personal Finance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a framework of personal money management concepts, including establishing values and goals, determining sources of income, managing income, preparing a budget, developing consumer buying ability, using credit, understanding savings and insurance, providing for adequate retirement, and estate planning.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Financial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic financial management topics including statement analysis, working capital; capital budgeting, and long-term financing. Focuses on Net Present Value and Internal Rate of Return techniques, lease vs. buy analysis, and Cost of Capital computations. Uses problems and cases to enhance skills in financial planning and decision making.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Forest and Wildlife Ecology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the interrelationships of organisms and the natural and cultural environments with emphasis on human influences, ecological structures, survey of populations, communities, and ecosystems.

courses.title: Wildlife and Fisheries Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the principles of wildlife and fisheries management. Emphasizes practices in the eastern United States.

courses.title: Forest Mensuration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: FOR 115 , MTH 113 , MTH 114
courses.description: Teaches principles of forest measurements including basic elements of property boundary, location, forest mapping, techniques of tree measurement, and saw log and pulp wood scaling.

courses.title: Applied Silviculture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: FOR 115
courses.description: Focuses on theory and practices involved in controlling the forest establishment, composition and growth. Laboratory emphasizes observation and application of various silvicultural procedures including site preparation, regeneration, and intermediate treatments.

courses.title: Beginning French I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning French II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school French, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Conversation in French I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part I of II.

courses.title: Conversation in French II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 .
courses.description: Emphasizes the spoken language, stressing fluency and correctness of structure, pronunciation, and vocabulary. Part II of II.

courses.title: Intermediate French I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Part I of II.

courses.title: Intermediate French I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Emergency Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview to fire protection; career opportunities in fire protection and related fields; philosophy and history of fire protection/service; fire loss analysis; organization and function to public and private fire protection services; fire departments as part of local government; laws and regulations affecting the fire service; fire service nomenclature; specific fire protection functions; basic fire chemistry and physics; introduction to fire protection systems; introduction to fire strategy and tactics.

courses.title: Fire Behavior and Combustion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the theories and fundamentals of how and why fires start, spread, and how they are controlled.

courses.title: Hazardous Materials Chemistry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides basic fire chemistry relating to the categories of hazardous materials including problems of recognition, reactivity, and health encountered by firefighters.

courses.title: Fire Prevention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides fundamental information regarding the history and philosophy of fire prevention, organization and operation of a fire prevention bureau, use of fire codes, identification and correction of fire hazards, and the relationships of fire prevention with built-in fire protection systems, fire investigation, and fire and life-safety education.

courses.title: Occupational Safety and Health for the Fire Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic concepts of occupational health and safety as it relates to emergency service organizations. Includes risk evaluation and control procedures for fire stations, training sites, emergency vehicles, and emergency situations involving fire, EMS, hazardous materials, and technical rescue. (Upon completion of this course, students should be able to establish and manage a safety program in an emergency service organization.

courses.title: Fire Protection Hydraulics and Water Supply
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation of theoretical knowledge in order to understand the principles of the use of water in fire protection and to apply hydraulic principles to analyze and to solve water supply problems.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Fire Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the Federal, State, and local laws that regulate emergency services, national standards influencing emergency services,, standard of care, tort, liability, and a review of relevant court cases.

courses.title: Building Construction for Fire Protection
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the components of building construction that relate to fire and life safety. Focuses on firefighter safety. Covers the elements of construction and design of structures and how they are key factors when inspecting buildings, preplanning fire operations, and operating at emergencies.

courses.title: Strategy and Tactics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth analysis of the principles of fire control through utilization of personnel, equipment, and extinguishing agents on the fire ground.

courses.title: Fire and Risk Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FST 240 .
courses.description: Presents a study of current urban fire problems with emphasis on solutions based upon current available technology. Includes master planning, as well as methods of identifying, analyzing and measuring accompanying risk and loss possibilities.

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the global patterns and processes of the atmosphere, biosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere. Explores Earth?s physical systems and the interrelationships among them through studying Earth-Sun geometry, climate and weather phenomena, landforms, biomes, and environmental change.

courses.title: People and the Land: Intro to Cultural Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to themes in human geography and the ways in which human geographers study spatial relationships in the world. Emphasizes geospatial tools and concepts to examine global patterns of human demographics, culture, geopolitics, and economic and environmental interdependence through introduction to a broad range of subject matter. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Regional Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines similarities and differences among the world's major regions. Evaluates ways in which people and places interact across space and time to produce particular spatial and environmental patterns. Introduces the student to geographic tools such as maps. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning German I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning German II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: GER 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school German, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Physical Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the science of physical geology through a comprehensive systems-based examination of Earth's structure, composition, rocks and minerals, landforms, geomorphology, and agents responsible for shaping and modifying its environments. Explores the origin and evolution of Earth's topographic and bathymetric features, geologic phenomena, and geologic hazards, resulting from plate tectonics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Earth Systems: An Environmental Geology Perspective
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts in earth systems including earth materials, plate tectonics, weathering, surface and groundwater, wasting, volcanoes, earthquakes and coastal, as well as pollution and climate change. Explores major topics relating human interaction with the physical environment through case studies. Reinforces applications through laboratory experiments, demonstrations, and field studies. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Oceanography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part I of II.

courses.title: Oceanography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part II of II.

courses.title: Environmental Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: GOL 105 .
courses.description: Explores the interaction between man and his physical environment. Stresses geologic hazards and environmental pollution utilizing case histories.

courses.title: Medical Terminology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the language used in the health record. Includes a system-by-system review of anatomical disease, and operative terms, abbreviations, radiography procedures, laboratory tests, and pharmacology terms. Part I of II.

courses.title: Reimbursement Issues in Medical Practice Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces major reimbursement systems in the United States. Focuses on prospective payment systems, managed care, and documentation necessary for appropriate reimbursement. Emphasizes management of practice to avoid fraud.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Pre-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from ancient times to 1600 CE. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Post-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from 1600 CE to the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Pre-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Europe from antiquity to approximately 1500. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Post-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas from approximately 1500 CE through the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from its origins to 1877. Includes the European exploration, development of the American colonies and their institutions, the Revolution, major political, social and economic developments, geographical expansion, the Civil War, and Reconstruction. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History Since 1865
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from 1865 to present. Includes major political, social and economic developments since 1865, overseas expansion, the two world wars, the Cold War and the post-Cold War era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Women in American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of women and attitudes toward women in American society from colonial times to the present.

courses.title: History of the Contemporary World
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes world developments since World War II.

courses.title: African-American History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of African Americans from their African origins to 1876.

courses.title: African-American History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of black Americans from their African origins to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Historical Archaeology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces both the methods and theories in historical archaeology as practiced in the United States and worldwide. Includes time and space, field survey, excavation, archival and laboratory research. Includes field trips to site excavations.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: History of African Civilization
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines major social, economic, political and religious developments across the African continent from earliest times to the present. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Topics in European History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the history of Europe from ancient times to the present. Part I of II.

courses.title: Topics in European History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the history of Europe from ancient times to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Latin American History
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of Latin American civilizations from the pre-Columbian era to the present

courses.title: History of Russia I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys history of Russia from earliest times to the present. Includes political, economic, multi-national, social, and cultural aspects of Russian and Soviet history. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Middle East Civilization I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys intellectual, cultural, social, economic and religious patterns in the civilizations of the Middle East. Covers Semitic, Indo-European, and Turkic-speaking peoples from pre-Islamic to the present. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of Middle East Civilization II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys intellectual, cultural, social, economic and religious patterns in the civilizations of the Middle East. Covers Semitic, Indo-European, and Turkic-speaking peoples from pre-Islamic to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: The American Constitution
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes the origin and development of the United States Constitution. Includes the evolution of civil liberties, property rights, contracts, due process, judicial review, federal-state relationships, and corporate-government relations.

courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies factors that led to the division between the States. Examines the war, the home fronts, and the era of Reconstruction.

courses.title: United States History Since World War II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates United States history from 1945 to the present, studying both domestic developments and American involvement in international affairs.

courses.title: The American Experience in Vietnam
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes American involvement in Vietnam from World War II with emphasis on the presidencies of Johnson, Nixon and Ford.

courses.title: American Foreign Policy Since 1890
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines American foreign policy since 1890 with an emphasis on current events and diverse points of view.

courses.title: History of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the cultural, economic, political, and religious history of Virginia from pre-contact to the present. Includes diverse perspectives to emphasize the significant contributions different groups of people (African Americans, Indigenous Peoples, European-Americans, Women) made to the history of Virginia, the colonies, and the United States.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Health Records Coding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of coding classification systems. Introduces ICD-9-CM coding classification system, its format and conventions. Stresses basic coding steps and guidelines according to body systems. Provides actual coding exercises in relation to each system covered.

courses.title: Advanced Coding and Reimbursement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses advanced coding skills through practical exercises using actual medical records. Introduces CPT-4 coding system and guidelines for out-patient/ambulatory surgery coding. Introduces prospective payment system and its integration with ICD-9-CM coding.

courses.title: First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety, first aid, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: First Aid and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety and first aid.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces and focuses on the principles of personal and community health.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal Wellness Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the dimensions of wellness including the physical, emotional, environmental, spiritual, occupational, and social components.

courses.title: Substance Abuse: Prevention and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the use and abuse of drugs in contemporary society with emphasis upon sociological, physiological, and psychological effects of drugs.

courses.title: Nutrition and Diet Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrients, sources, functions, and requirements with an introduction to diet therapy. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrient components of food, including carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals and water. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Orientation to Health Related Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1- 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the interrelated roles and functions of various members of the health team.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Medical Terminology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems, and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation, and usage. Emphasizes more complex skills and techniques in understanding medical terminology. Part II of II. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Ethics for Health Care Personnel
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on ethical concepts of health care. Emphasizes confidentiality, maintaining patient records, personal appearance, professionalism with patients/clients, associates, and an awareness of health care facilities.

courses.title: Cross Cultural Health and Wellness Practices
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores prevailing cultural values toward health and wellness and compares them with cultures around the world.Presents concepts related to communication, spirituality, family and gender roles, dietary restrictions, traditional practices, reaction to pain and end-of-life decisions.

courses.title: Current Issues and Health Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on current issues in the health care industry.

courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Women's Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores current issues related to women's health and wellness with an emphasis upon prevention of disease and optimum well being. Takes a multi-ethnic approach to exploring the most up-to-date findings, diagnostic tools, and treatments for breast cancer, reproductive tract illness, heart, and other common diseases faced by women from puberty through menopause.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of various forms of physical activity and how they promote human health. Examines the study of physical activity from the perspectives of professional practice, scholarly study and experience. Provides a broad overview of the history, scientific principles, methodologies, and research among the major subdisciplines to prepare students for further study in kinesiology and health sciences. Explores current issues, future directions, certifications, professional associations, and career opportunities.

courses.title: Personal Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of stress and explores its physical, psychological and social effects. Includes the relationships among stress and change, self-evaluation, sources of stress, and ways to develop current coping skills for handling stress. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Concepts of Disease
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general principles, classifications, causes, and treatments of selected disease processes. Intended primarily for students enrolled in health technology programs.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: General Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general pharmacology for the health related professions covering general principles of drug actions/reactions, major drug classes, specific agent within each class, and routine mathematical calculations needed to determine desired dosages.

courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per work.
courses.description: Expands the development of counseling skills needed to function effectively in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in responding, personalizing, summarizing and initiating. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement. Develops plans for achieving personal and program goals.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Effects of Psychoactive Drugs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides information on the biochemical, physiological, and behavioral aspects of substance addiction and will review the symptoms of addiction. Emphasizes areas of chemical dependency, medical epidemiology, physiological threats of addiction and methods of identifying multiple drug abusers.

courses.title: Professional Skill Development for Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teach professional skills necessary to make the transition from the role of MH consumer/client to that of services provider. Will cover confidentiality, professionalism, boundaries and roles, cultural diversity and personal values.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HMS 251 .
courses.description: Expands knowledge and skill in working with individuals with substance use disorder. Focuses on assisting people with substance use disorder in individual and group settings and explores client treatment modalities. May provide opportunities for field experience in treatment centers.

courses.title: Case Management and Substance Abuse
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the process for interviewing substance abuse clients. Includes intake, assessment, handling denial, and ending the interview. Teaches skills for writing short-term goals and treatment plans with emphasis on accountability. Examines various reporting devices.

courses.title: Human Behavior I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills in working with individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities within the socio- cultural context. Emphasizes historical development of various social systems and how these systems affect the whole person. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Food Service Managers Sanitation Certification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an accelerated survey of principles and applications of sanitary food service, designed to promote the skills of managers in food service establishments licensed by the Commonwealth of Virginia. (Upon successful completion of the course, a certificate of achievement is awarded by the Educational Foundation of the National Restaurant Association and the student's name is entered in the Foundation Registry.)

courses.title: Applied Nutrition for Food Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (HRI 122) may be required as identified by the college.
courses.description: Studies food composition, nutrition science, and application of nutrition principles by the food service professional. Provides the student with a basic understanding of human nutrition and application of nutrition in the service of commercially prepared meals.

courses.title: Principles of Baking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of breads, pastries, baked desserts, candies, frozen confections, and sugar work. Applies scientific principles and techniques of baking. Promotes the knowledge/skills required to prepare baked items, pastries and confections.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Service Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a conceptual and technical framework for managing the service of meals in a variety of commercial settings. Studies the integration of production and service delivery, guest contact dynamics, reservations management and point-of-sale systems.

courses.title: Commercial Food Production Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches commercial cooking. Studies management's role in setting up and running commercial cooking operations, menu planning, menu evaluation, standardization of recipes, and scheduling of manpower.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Quality for the Hospitality Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches quality in the hospitality industry, including material on the total quality management movement. Emphasizes quality from the customer's perspective.

courses.title: Garde Manger
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies garde manger, the art of decorative cold food preparation and presentation. Provides a detailed practical study of cold food preparation and artistic combination and display of cold foods.

courses.title: American Regional Cuisine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the distinct regional cooking styles of America and its neighbors. Emphasizes the indigenous ingredients as well as the cultural aspect of each region's cooking style. Includes the preparation of the various regional foods.

courses.title: Fruit, Vegetable, and Starch Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of fruits, vegetables, grains, cereals, legumes and farinaceous products. Promotes the knowledge/skills necessary to prepare menu items from fruits, vegetables, and their byproducts, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Stock, Soup, and Sauce Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of stocks, soups, and sauces. Promotes the knowledge/skills to prepare stocks, soups, and sauces, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Menu Planning and Dining Room Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers fundamentals of menu writing, types of menus, layout, design and food merchandising, and interpreting a profit and loss statement as it relates to menu pricing. Analyzes menus for effectiveness. Instructs on proper dining room service, customer seating, and dining room management. Emphasizes use of computer in management of food service operations.

courses.title: Marketing of Hospitality Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and practices of marketing the services of the hotel and restaurant industry. Emphasizes the marketing concept with applications leading to customer satisfaction. Reviews methods of external and internal stimulation of sales. May include a practical sales/marketing exercise and computer applications.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Cost Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents methods of pre-cost and pre-control as applied to the menu, purchasing, receiving, storing, issuing, production, sales and service which result in achievement of an operation's profit potential. Emphasizes both manual and computerized approaches. Part I of II.

courses.title: Human Res. Mgmt, and Trng. for Hospi. and Tourism
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the students for interviewing, training and developing employees. Covers management skills (technical, human, and conceptual) and leadership. Covers the establishment and use of effective training and evaluative tools to improve productivity. Emphasizes staff and customer relations.

courses.title: Principles and Applications of Catering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Analyzes and compares the principles of on-premise and off- premise catering. Includes student presentations in a series of catered functions where they assume typical managerial/employee positions emphasizing planning, organizing, operating, managing and evaluating.

courses.title: Catering Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies special functions in the hospitality industry. Presents lecture and demonstration in banquet layout, menus, services, sales and supervision.

courses.title: Hospitality Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies legal principles governing hospitality operations. Includes applications of common law and statutory decisions, discussion of legal theory, and regulations governing management of hospitality enterprise.

courses.title: Artisan Breads
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an integrated study of both classical and modern baking methods. Focuses on craft baking using simple ingredients to create superior products.

courses.title: European Tortes and Cakes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: HRI 280 .
courses.description: Provides an integrated study of European tortes and cakes.

courses.title: Custards and Cremes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: HRI 280 .
courses.description: Provides an integrated study of classical and contemporary custards and cremes as menu items and recipe ingredients.

courses.title: Health-Conscious Baking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with an understanding of the ingredients and methods used in creating healthy and special needs breads, pastries, cookies, and other desserts.

courses.title: Introduction to Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces commercial horticulture industry with emphasis on career opportunities. Examines equipment, facilities, and physical arrangements of production, wholesale and retail establishments. Surveys individual areas within horticulture industry.

courses.title: Practical Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience in landscape construction equipment operations and maintenance.

courses.title: Principles of Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts of plant growth and development. Covers horticultural practices, crops and environmental factors affecting plant growth.

courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of plant propagation. Examines commercial and home practices. Provides experience in techniques using seed-spores, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering and division.

courses.title: History of Garden Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the development of gardens as they chronicle the development of civilization. Introduces the periods, in both Europe and North America, beginning with settlement, on through industrial development, land and space utilization to current environmental concerns. Explores physical and cultural influences on garden design and utilization.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Chemicals in Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes basic chemical principles and their application to horticulture. Introduces principles of inorganic and organic chemicals. Studies chemical activities of insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, fertilizers, and growth regulators.

courses.title: Home Landscaping
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies current approaches to improving home landscapes. Emphasizes planning, proper implementation, and landscape maintenance.

courses.title: Horticultural Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies taxonomy, anatomy, morphology, physiology, and genetics of plants as applied to identification, propagation and culture.

courses.title: Landscape Plants I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Landscape Plants II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part II of II.

courses.title: Plant Pest Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of plant pest management. Covers morphology and life cycles of insects and other small animal pests and plant pathogens. Lab stresses diagnosis, chemical and non-chemical control of specific pests, and pesticide safety.

courses.title: Turfgrass Management I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies scientific principles for the establishment and maintenance of intensely managed turfgrass. Topics covered include cultivar selection, seeding, sprigging and sodding techniques, fertilization, watering, weed identification and control, insect identification and control, fungus identification and control, soil structure, drainage, topdressing, and mowing frequency and height.

courses.title: Site Analysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines basic landscape and site planning techniques, environmental considerations and construction principles.

courses.title: Landscape Drawing Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies theories of landscape design and drawing to actual design projects and tasks. Emphasizes drawing techniques and use of advanced media in applications. Includes hard line, free-style, and computer-assisted landscape drawing in simple landscape drawing applications.

courses.title: Landscape Drawing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches students the use of drafting equipment. Emphasizes drawing techniques and use of media. Includes hard line and free-style landscape drawing.

courses.title: Herbaceous Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies identification, culture and uses of herbaceous plants in landscaping. Includes perennials, biennials, common bulbs and annuals. Teaches scientific and common names of plants.

courses.title: Indoor Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies identification, culture, and uses of indoor plants in interior landscaping. Includes tropical, subtropical and non-hardy temperate plants. Teaches scientific and common names of plants.

courses.title: Introduction to Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of basic table arrangements. Includes the history of design styles, identification of flowers and green, identification and use of equipment, and conditioning and handling of flowers.

courses.title: Advanced Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for composition of traditional floral designs and contemporary floral designs. Includes use of exotic florals to create arrangement styles such as Japanese, European and Williamsburg.

courses.title: Landscape Construction and Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines practical applications of commercial landscape construction techniques, and materials used. Covers construction, planting, and maintenance.

courses.title: Management of a Horticultural Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the business and selling practices which relate to wholesale and retail horticultural businesses including garden centers, greenhouses, nurseries, and flower shops. Examines planning and layout, suppliers, merchandising, maintenance, and display of horticultural items.

courses.title: Great Books I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part I of II.

courses.title: Controversial Issues in Contemporary American Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to selected issues in contemporary American culture. Includes topic areas ranging from welfare reform, economic development, privacy, environmental protection and conservation, evolution vs. creation, to family values, and special interest lobbying in our state and national governments. Focuses on the development of the student's critical thinking skills by analyzing, evaluating, and reflecting on opposing sides of the same issue as expressed by public leaders, special interest groups and academicians.

courses.title: Early Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from prehistory up to the 1300s, integrating the arts, literature, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an interdisciplinary approach to the study of African-American life, history, and culture. Examines specific events, ideologies, and individuals that have shaped the contours of African-American life. Studies the history, sociology, economics, religion, politics, psychology, creative productions, and culture of African- Americans. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Creative Thinking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines, analyzes, and develops creative and critical thinking processes with individual and group applications to solve business, scientific, social, environmental, and other practical problems. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: The Greek and Roman Tradition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the significance of Greek and Roman cultures on the individual and society, expressed prominently from the Classical Age in Athens to its survival during Roman times. Examines the key contributions that the Greeks and Romans have imparted upon storytelling, theater, philosophy, civics, political morphology, and the arts and the impact they have in the modern world. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Quality Assurance Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and techniques of quality engineering for the management, design engineering economics, production, and assurance of quality. Emphasizes fundamentals of total quality assurance for product and process control. May include design review, fundamentals of statistics procurement control, sampling and control chart systems, quality reporting, process capability analysis, tool and gauge control, document control, or troubleshooting quality control. Part I of II.

courses.title: Industrial Methods
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers theoretical knowledge necessary for familiarization with common handtools, common power tools, measuring tools and techniques, fastening components and procedures, grinding operations, metal cutting operations, and other miscellaneous tasks.

courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials.

courses.title: Applied Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic information and problem solving techniques in liquids, gases, solids, metrics, mechanics, forces, simple machines, heat, light, sound and nuclear energy as applied in industrial engineering technologies.

courses.title: Industrial Supervision I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concept of the Supervisor as a Leader. Discusses the role of the Industrial Supervisor in the face of technology advances. Discusses the role of the Industrial Supervisor in leading organizational change and helping employees through transitions. Defines Leadership styles and the selection of the appropriate style. Introduces the Industrial Supervisor as a motivator in terms of job satisfaction, morale, job design competition, communication, and promotions. Presents ethical behavior and dilemmas in organizations.

courses.title: Installation and Preventive Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies practices in the installation of machinery, including mounting, grouting, leveling, and alignment. Examines methods of preventive maintenance including inspection, scheduled maintenance, controls, record keeping, repair parts stocking, and safety considerations.

courses.title: Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, structure, and organization of the quality control unit. May include incoming material control, product and process control, and cost control.

courses.title: Industrial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies planning, organizing, directing, and influencing industrial activities. May include research, product design, methods and time management, quality assurance and current manufacturing methodologies.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.`
courses.description: Introduces principle concepts of technology involving mechanical, fluid, electrical, and thermal power as they relate to force, work, and rate.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: IND 165 .
courses.description: Introduces principle concepts of technology involving mechanical, fluid, electrical, and thermal power as they relate to resistance, energy, power, and force transformers. Places an emphasis on mechanical and advantage systems.
